code_at_head_verified.method: sha256 of git show <commit>:<file>, compared with the registered code_at_head; the new files modify none of them

implementation_notes: Subsets: the job writes each ids file from the JSON's ids list once (an existing file must be byte-identical), after asserting it equals the rule's prefix (train_rl.schedule over all 3469 ids of train minus dev300, seed 42; floor(3469 x pct / 100) ids), holds no dev300 image and has its registered sha256; build_gold_sft.py (unchanged) builds the SFT rows and `sha256sum -c registered.sha256` asserts the ids files and the registered sft.jsonl sha256 before any training.

Step 0 first: p1dev_s42 is re-decoded on the job's machine as p1dev_s42_redecode (evaluate.py, short prompt, bf16, its defaults) before any training; it is the 100% point of every fit. Its agreement with the registered n2 decode (identical captions; CIDEr-D difference) is written to scaling.json and selects nothing.

Metrics on dev300 for p1dev_s42_f25, p1dev_s42_f50 and p1dev_s42_redecode: CIDEr-D x100 is the mean of rl_report.dev_scores per-image values (dev_scores asserts that mean equals evaluate.py's corpus CIDEr-D within 1e-6, and each result must be scored with rdrsegmenter); object F1 is object_prf.scores' exact-class F1 against the union of the five references' classes; CHAIR_i is rescap.chair's, called as evaluate.py calls it, and must equal each result's own CHAIR_i.

Bootstrap: one index draw numpy.random.default_rng(0).integers(0, 300, (2000, 300)), the draw rl_reward.boot makes, shared by the three models; per draw each corpus metric is recomputed (CIDEr-D mean, object_prf F1, hallucinated over all mentions) and the OLS slope on log2(N) refitted; the 95% interval is numpy.percentile at 2.5 and 97.5. One training seed per size, so it covers dev-image sampling only.

Decision: decide(b, CI_lo) evaluates the registered clauses in their written order: FUND_EXTERNAL_IMAGE_DATA if CI_lo(b) > +1, else CLOSE_DATA_VOLUME_LEVERS if b < +1, else INCONCLUSIVE; b is the full-sample OLS slope of CIDEr-D x100 on log2(N) (per doubling). The frozen predictions are reported as hits (bounds inclusive) and decide nothing.

Before any verdict, --analyse recomputes the registered n2 decode's P, R and F1 vs ktvic5 (to the registered three decimals), CHAIR_i and mentions per caption and exits unless they equal p1dev_reference_dev300.

Guards: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 with refs/main naming cc594898 and the five registered shard sha256, so the checked snapshot is the base every from_pretrained loads; NCS_DATASET and RESCAP_* are unset (the hook's defaults: save_steps 200, save_total_limit 2); each training log must show the hook (save_steps=200), the card rule (512 vision tokens, 4-bit) and 'loss mask: assistant'; each adapter's LoRA config must equal the registered r, alpha, dropout and target_modules on the registered base; the job file must carry the registered train/decode flags and none of --four-bit, --max-new-tokens, --max-vision-tokens, --limit or test_data.json.

Nothing is overwritten: a step whose output exists is skipped; training resumes from the hook's checkpoints; if a decode was saved but its scoring failed, the job scores the saved predictions (evaluate.py --predictions) instead of decoding again; scaling.json goes to the next _vN if it exists.

Outputs in /root/outputs/t3_4_s5_data_scaling/: ids files and registered.sha256, SFT rows, the three dev300 results with evaluate.py's .preds.json and the hook's .provenance.json, training logs, scaling.json (with machine_id, git_head_sha and the hook sha) and SHA256SUMS, which also lists the two new adapters' final files in $NCS_DATA/runs (qrun's post-job stamp copies those to /root/outputs/runs).
